name: soft-key-goal
task: Grab the key, and after that get to the goal square if you can.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands getting to the goal after acquiring the key if possible, but both the goal requirement and its order are soft. Make Precedence(has_key, at_goal) and Existence(at_goal) hard; keep Existence(has_key) hard.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Existence(has_key) is correct, but the task makes reaching the goal conditional on “if you can.” The hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) adds a hard order requirement from that preference-scoped phrase. Make the Precedence soft; keep the soft Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Existence(has_key) requires acquiring the key, but the task says to get the goal square only “if you can,” and does not require acquiring the key unconditionally. Make the key requirement soft or remove it. The soft Precedence(has_key, at_goal) and soft Existence(at_goal) correctly reflect the conditional preference.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Existence(has_key) correctly captures “Grab the key.” But both goal clauses are soft even though “get to the goal square” is commanded; “if you can” makes reaching the goal a preference, but does not make the stated order “after that” optional. The soft Precedence(has_key, at_goal) weakens that order. Make Precedence(has_key, at_goal) hard and keep Existence(at_goal) soft.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) and soft Existence(at_goal) both come from “get to the goal square if you can,” but that goal is only preferred. The task says to get to the goal after grabbing the key; it does not require that order as a hard rule. Make the precedence soft, like the goal preference. Keep hard Existence(has_key) and soft Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Existence(has_key) adds a requirement to acquire the key, but “Grab the key” does command that, so it is correct. The soft Existence(at_goal) correctly reflects “if you can.” However, the hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) makes reaching the goal conditional on having acquired the key, which the task does not state: “after that” links the commanded goal step to grabbing the key, but the goal is only preferred. Remove the hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal); keep the two Existence clauses.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task says to get to the goal after acquiring the key “if you can,” so the goal preference is soft, but the order “after that” is unconditional. The soft Precedence(has_key, at_goal) weakens that required order. Make it hard; keep the hard Existence(has_key) and soft Existence(at_goal).

NO CHANGES NEEDED: The hard Existence(has_key) requires grabbing the key. The goal and its order after acquiring the key are both conditional on “if you can,” so the soft Existence(at_goal) and soft Precedence(has_key, at_goal) correctly express those preferences.

texts: Reach the goal square, if possible.
Reach the goal square after acquiring the key, if possible.
